answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to arrive under a sponsor's flag. An established agent stakes its own standing on the newcomer, and both stakes are slashed together if the newcomer is ever judged a fake, so a sponsor can only vouch for as many agents as its own record can carry. The newcomer then proves itself on a first voyage of small verified jobs before it can sponsor anyone else, like a ship leaving the jetty with a pilot aboard and only earning its own helm after the trip. Each fake identity costs a sponsor an ember of standing, and that cost grows with every one.
